::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How do I set a variable inside of \rlap](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/7672/how-do-i-set-a-variable-inside-of-rlap), asked by [srking](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/2528/srking) on TeX Stack Exchange (2010-12-24; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> Two questions please about this code example:
>
> 1) Why does `\rlap` prevent me from setting a variable?<br>
> 2) How do I set a variable from within an `\rlap` that is visible outside of `\rlap`?
>
> I'm using MikTex 2.8.  Thanks for any clue!
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> \newif\ifmycheck
> \begin{document}
> \rlap{\mychecktrue}
> % \mychecktrue
> \ifmycheck
> Check True!
> \else
> Check False!  % always takes this path!
> \fi
> \end{document}
> ```
:::

1.  Changes within a group stay inside that group, and `\rlap` puts its argument inside an `\hbox`, therefore within its own group.  So if you did:

        \rlap{\mychecktrue % group is still open!
        % \mychecktrue
        \ifmycheck
        Check True!
        \else
        Check False!  
        \fi}

  You will get 
>Check True!

  So you see that you did set the variable inside `\rlap`.  

2. You want the changes to persist outside the group.  So use the prefix `\global`:

        \rlap{\global\mychecktrue}
        % \mychecktrue
        \ifmycheck
        Check True!
        \else
        Check False!  
        \fi

  That will result again in "Check True!"
